name: light-code-vscode
description: A minimal agentic coding assistant. Bring your own model. No telemetry, no default endpoints.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Light Code
walkthroughs.description: Point it at a model, then turn on only the parts you want.

steps.title: Point it at a model
steps.description:
Light Code ships with no endpoints — a fresh install contacts nothing until you configure a provider.
[Open Light Code](command:lightCode.openPanel)

steps.title: Ask for something real
steps.description:
One tool call at a time, with the result in front of you. Attach files, read documents, page through logs.
[Open Light Code](command:lightCode.openPanel)

steps.title: Nothing happens without you
steps.description:
Every edit and command is shown as ground truth before it runs — and Deny is a real answer.
[Open Light Code](command:lightCode.openPanel)

steps.title: Connect the servers you already run
steps.description:
MCP over stdio or HTTP. Their tools become ordinary tools, with the same approval prompt.
[Open Light Code](command:lightCode.openPanel)

steps.title: Let it write tools, and teach it your codebase
steps.description:
Python tools pinned to the source you approved, and skills that cost a line of context each.
[Open Light Code](command:lightCode.openPanel)

steps.title: Find things by meaning
steps.description:
Semantic search over your code, against a local Qdrant or Chroma, or an OpenSearch cluster.
[Open Light Code](command:lightCode.openPanel)

steps.title: Spend less on the hard parts
steps.description:
A cheap model does the work and consults Claude for the plan, inside a budget you set.
[Open Light Code](command:lightCode.openPanel)

steps.title: Let it run on its own
steps.description:
Prompts that run unattended, each with its own explicit list of tools.
[Open Light Code](command:lightCode.openPanel)

steps.title: What it does not do
steps.description:
No telemetry, no default endpoints, no sandboxing — and why each of those is stated plainly.
[Open Light Code](command:lightCode.openPanel)
